Reasoning effort that is raised for the next stage when a trigger fires

Source: R/core-effort-escalate.R
hr_effort_escalate.Rd

A policy for a call's effort (hr_call()) or a read's effort_mode (gr_read_spec()). Every stage starts at base (one level, or a map named by call stem, resolved as a static effort is). When a trigger in on fired during a stage, the next stage is sent at to. The stage after a raised one goes back to base unless a trigger fired in the raised stage too and a raise is left: at most max_escalations raises happen in one run (one trace), so at the default of 1 it always goes back. A stage is a call label up to its second dot, with a merge level (.level2), a summary level (.L2) and a judge's order (.o2) left off, so map.answer and reduce are stages and reduce.level1 belongs to reduce.

Usage

hr_effort_escalate(
  base = "low",
  to = "high",
  on = .hr_escalate_triggers,
  max_escalations = 1L,
  replies = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_effort_escalate'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

base

The starting effort: one level, or a character vector named by call stem.

to

The raised effort, one level.

on

The triggers that raise the next stage.

max_escalations

The most raises in one run.

replies

NULL, or a named character vector from trigger name to the text a reply that signals it starts with.

x

An hr_effort_escalate.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class hr_effort_escalate.

Details

The triggers the core sees for itself are "truncated" (a "truncate" step of the trace, or a reply cut off at its output cap; a cut made while a stage packs its requests belongs to that stage, including one made before its first request), "parse_failure" (a reply to a structured request, such as ctx$call_json(), that is not JSON) and "schema_failure" (one that does not fit the schema). replies names replies that are triggers: a named character vector from trigger to the text a reply starts with, such as c(not_in_document = "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT"); such a trigger fires when every request of the stage replied with it. Other triggers ("verify_failed", "unclear", "disagreement", or any name of your own) fire when the caller reports them with hr_effort_event().

The state lives on the run's trace, so a call without a trace is sent at base. Each raise writes an "effort.escalate" step naming the triggers, the stage they fired in and the stage raised; when the raised stage ends, an "effort.resolve" step says whether it fired the same triggers again. hr_effort_log() returns both as a table.

See also

hr_effort_event(), hr_effort_log(), hr_effort_check(), gr_read_spec() for effort_mode

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_condensation_check(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_reverse_text(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_chain(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_effort_check(), hr_effort_event(), hr_effort_log(), hr_mdd(), hr_modules(), hr_reference(), hr_register(), hr_report(), hr_scorer(), hr_set(), hr_settings(), hr_skill(), hr_step(), hr_step_command(), hr_sweep(), hr_sweep_check()

Examples

pol <- hr_effort_escalate(base = "low", to = "high",
                          replies = c(not_in_document = "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT"))
pol
#> <hr_effort_escalate>
#>   base: low; raised to high for the next stage, at most 1 time(s) a run
#>   on:   truncated, parse_failure, schema_failure, verify_failed, not_in_document, unclear, disagreement

# A first stage that found nothing raises the second.
cl <- hr_mock_client(function(m, p) {
  if (identical(p$effort, "low") && grepl("first", m[[1]]$content)) {
    return("NOT_IN_DOCUMENT")
  }
  paste("done at", p$effort)
})
tr <- hr_trace()
hr_call(cl, "first step", model = "gpt-5.6-luna", trace = tr, label = "plan.draft",
        effort = pol)$text
#> [1] "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT"
hr_call(cl, "second step", model = "gpt-5.6-luna", trace = tr, label = "plan.final",
        effort = pol)$text
#> [1] "done at high"
hr_effort_log(tr)
#>        after      stage        triggers   to calls resolved
#> 1 plan.draft plan.final not_in_document high     1     TRUE
